experiment.name: Does IL-8 go in opposite directions with severity in B. rossi and B. canis? Within-file contrasts and the Beagle course around treatment
experiment.description: Is the reported IL-8 conflict (lower with severity in B. rossi, higher in complicated B. canis) present in the dog-level files, and could sampling time after treatment or the severity definition explain it? Hypothesis: timing or definition is a sufficient explanation.

selection.S-CB017: infected day 1 (31), controls 16; day 7 (30) in check C2
selection.DS02: 5 Beagles; cytokines on days -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8; treatment after the day-4 sample

experiment.summary: No IL-8 conflict inside the dog-level files: severe minus non-severe Cliff's delta +0.02 (-0.28 to +0.34; S-CB050, died 12 vs survived 85) and +0.15 (-0.29 to +0.56; S-CB017, complicated 18 vs uncomplicated 13); DS02 shows no consistent post-treatment IL-8 change (R1 not met, R3 not met). 3 of 12 analyte tests passed BH q < 0.05 (IL-2 in S-CB017, GM-CSF in S-CB017, MCP-1 in S-CB017).

payload.label: IL-8, severe minus non-severe, inside each file
payload.headline: Verdict by the pre-stated rule: no conflict. Both IL-8 intervals include 0 and both point estimates are positive. The B. rossi fall in IL-8 is a contrast of infected dogs against healthy controls (delta -0.45), not of dogs that died against survivors. DS02 gives no support for a treatment-driven reversal.

sections.heading: Question
paragraphs: IL-8 is reported to fall with severity in B. rossi and to rise in complicated B. canis. Can sampling time (before treatment in S-CB050; 6-8 h after imidocarb in S-CB017) or the severity definition (death against 'complicated') explain the difference?

sections.heading: What was done
paragraphs: Inside each dog-level file, each of 6 shared analytes (IL-2, IL-8, IL-10, IL-18, GM-CSF, MCP-1) was compared between severe and non-severe dogs with Cliff's delta (bootstrap 95% CI by dog, permutation p, BH within each file, family of 6). DS02 (5 Beagles) gave the within-dog course before treatment and the change from day 4 to day 6, judged by three rules fixed in spec.md (R1 same direction in every dog, R2 larger than day-to-day change, R3 larger rise in the high-dose dogs). Checks: C1 IL-8 against WBC (the 'complicated' label uses SIRS, which uses WBC); C2 the S-CB017 day-7 contrast; S2 floors at half the floor.

Deviation D1 (added after the outcome lock, uses no outcome): infected dogs against the healthy controls of each file. It was added because the primary result showed no severity conflict, and the article notes place the B. rossi IL-8 fall between infected dogs and controls.

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: S-CB050 (B. rossi, admission, before treatment): IL-8 Cliff's delta +0.02 (95% CI -0.28 to +0.34), died 12 vs survived 85, medians 1172 vs 1066 pg/mL, permutation p 0.898.

S-CB017 (B. canis, day 1, 6-8 h after imidocarb): IL-8 Cliff's delta +0.15 (95% CI -0.29 to +0.56), complicated 18 vs uncomplicated 13, medians 908 vs 601 pg/mL, permutation p 0.518. At day 7 the S-CB017 estimate is -0.15 (-0.59 to +0.29).

Verdict by the pre-stated rule: no conflict. Neither file shows an IL-8 difference by severity, and both estimates are slightly positive. The severity direction that both files share is MCP-1: delta +0.47 (+0.22 to +0.70, q 0.052) and +0.81 (+0.56 to +0.97, q < 0.001). 3 of 12 tests passed q < 0.05 (IL-2 in S-CB017, GM-CSF in S-CB017, MCP-1 in S-CB017).

Where the IL-8 directions do differ is infection against health (deviation D1): infected minus controls -0.45 (-0.65 to -0.24) in S-CB050 (median 1066 vs 3317 pg/mL) and +0.87 (+0.68 to +1.00) in S-CB017. This difference cannot be separated from species, assay run and control selection.

DS02, IL-8 log2 change day 4 to day 6: d001 +1.80, d002 -0.23, d004 -2.33, d005 +1.09. R1 same direction in all 4 dogs: no; R2 median |change| 1.45 log2 against median day-to-day change before treatment 1.11: larger; R3 rises more in the high-dose dogs: no (mean change high dose -1.28, low dose +1.45). So DS02 does not support a treatment-driven reversal. Before treatment, IL-8 log2 change from baseline to day 4 by dog: d001 (low) +0.01, d002 (high) +1.65, d003 (high) +3.53, d004 (high) +1.04, d005 (low) -0.46. It rose in every high-dose dog, so in experimental B. rossi IL-8 went up, not down, as disease progressed.

C1: IL-8 correlated with WBC among infected dogs in S-CB050 (rho +0.30, +0.09 to +0.49) and in S-CB017 (rho +0.25, -0.11 to +0.57); the WBC difference by label had an interval that included 0 in both files (delta +0.11 and +0.23). The definition is therefore not needed to explain an IL-8 conflict that the files do not show.

sections.heading: What this does not show
paragraphs: The B. rossi report of IL-8 falling with severity rests on CB037 (55 dogs, a separate cohort with no dog-level file, read from the abstract only). This package cannot test it. In the one B. rossi dog-level file, IL-8 does not differ between dogs that died and survivors.
Detectable effect at 80% power: about 0.86 SD in S-CB050 (12 vs 85) and 1.05 SD in S-CB017 (18 vs 13). A smaller IL-8 difference is not excluded.

DS02 samples are daily; the first post-treatment cytokine sample is 36 to 48 h after treatment. A 6 to 8 h effect of imidocarb cannot be seen. DS02 has 4 dogs with a post-treatment sample and no severity label; dose group is a design variable.

Species, source, country, assay run, definition and sampling time are fully aliased between files. Nothing here attributes a difference to species. Died includes euthanasia for poor prognosis. This is a descriptive re-analysis of comparisons that were already published.
